DC circuit loop

Battery voltage and current converted directly into watts

DC pages need a clean loop: battery, load, current direction, and watts without power factor.

Formula Watts = Amps x 12V

Quick answer

Use this calculator when DC current and voltage convert directly into watts.

DC systems do not use power factor, so the calculation is direct. This is useful for batteries, automotive systems, LED drivers, electronics, and solar DC accessories.

Watts = Amps x 12V

Inputs to check before calculating

  • Use measured voltage when battery voltage is above or below nominal.
  • Enter continuous current for heat and runtime planning.
  • Check fuse and wire ratings against the calculated current.
  • For battery loads, convert watts into Wh for runtime estimates.

Example: 10 amps at 12 volts

At 12 volts, 10 amps equals 120 watts before AC power-factor adjustments. Formula: 10 A x 12 V = 120 W.

Best use cases

  • Battery and vehicle systems
  • DC mode by default
  • Instant wattage and kW output
  • DC load planning with clear unit labels.

Common mistake to avoid

Do not assume a 12V battery is always exactly 12.0V; charging and resting voltage can change the watt result.

How to use the result

Use the watt output to compare loads, size power supplies, and estimate battery energy use.

Accuracy and safety note

Calculator output is a planning estimate. Final breaker sizing, wire gauge, derating, voltage-drop limits, equipment protection, and code compliance should be verified with manufacturer documentation and a qualified electrician or engineer.

Methodology, Review Notes, and Sources

How this calculator works

The calculator applies Watt's law for DC and resistive loads, then adds power factor for AC loads and the 1.732 multiplier for balanced three-phase line-to-line calculations.

  • DC and resistive loads: W = A x V
  • Single-phase AC: W = A x V x PF
  • Three-phase AC: W = 1.732 x A x V x PF

FAQ

12V Calculator FAQ

Fast answers before you use the calculator or compare formulas.

W How do I convert 12V amps to watts?

Multiply the current in amps by 12 volts. For example, 5 amps at 12V equals 60 watts (5 × 12 = 60). DC conversions do not require a power factor because current and voltage are always in phase.

BAT How many watts can a 12V battery deliver?

A 12V battery's power output depends on current draw. At 10A, it delivers 120W. At 20A, it delivers 240W. The maximum safe current depends on the battery's internal resistance, terminal rating, and fuse protection. Always check the battery data sheet for maximum discharge rate.

DC Why is DC conversion simpler than AC?

DC circuits have no power factor because current and voltage don't alternate. The formula is simply Watts = Amps × Volts. AC circuits have reactive power from inductors and capacitors that requires a power factor correction, making the formula Watts = Amps × Volts × PF.

AWG What wire gauge do I need for 12V DC?

Wire gauge for 12V DC depends on current, distance, and acceptable voltage drop. Low-voltage DC circuits are especially sensitive to voltage drop because a 0.5V loss is a larger percentage of 12V than of 120V. Use the wire gauge calculator with one-way distance and 12V to find the right conductor size.

PV Can I use this calculator for solar panel circuits?

Yes, but use the correct voltage point. Solar panels operate at Vmp (maximum power voltage), not the battery voltage. A 12V-nominal panel may have Vmp of 17–18V. For battery-side current, use the battery voltage. For panel-side wiring, use the panel Vmp.

RUN How do I calculate battery runtime from watts at 12V?

First convert amps to watts (A × 12V). Then convert battery capacity: Watt-hours = Amp-hours × 12V. Divide Wh by the load watts to estimate runtime in hours. Account for inverter efficiency (typically 85–92%) if converting DC to AC. Use the amp-hours to watt-hours calculator for detailed estimates.
